item: The story read streams 900 articles at a time and keeps the richest 4,000 in a heap, so its memory follows the chunk and not the corpus
summary: build_stories read every mention row of the period with one .all() and only then kept the 4,000 richest articles, so the read's memory grew with the corpus (resident rise 3,650 MB plain at 12.48 M mentions; Python heap 417.8 MB at 1.56 M, about 268 B a mention row). The period's article ids now come from ix_article_observed (8 B each), mentions are read 900 articles at a time through the covering index ix_mention_article_count, each article is cut to its top 12 visible keywords as it arrives and a heap keeps the richest 4,000. On a world whose mention dates agree with the article clock the kept sets are identical: one digest across all six written cells, old and new, at chunk 100, 300 and 900. Measured on written corpora of 1.56 to 12.48 M mentions (4 vCPU 2.1 GHz, Python 3.13.12): resident rise 0.26 to 0.31 GB plain and 0.10 to 0.13 GB encrypted at every size, Python heap 417.8 MB to 45.7 MB, cold read 1.3x faster at 20 k articles and 1.9x at 160 k (72.1 s to 38.0 s); chunk 900 is the fastest of 100/300/900. The read runs under statement_deadline (default 600 s, OO_BULLETIN_STORIES_DEADLINE_S, clamped to 3,600): measured 3.0 us a row cold, extrapolated (labelled) to 64 s at the field's 20.9 M rows. The payload carries read_bound. Quarantined articles stay in the read (D22 removes them) and stand-ins stay out. TWO STATED DIFFERENCES, each pinned by a test: an article is in the period by its own clock (coalesce(published_at, created_at), period.py's definition) where the old read followed each mention's stamped observed_on, so an article whose clock moved after it was indexed (the law corpus heal clears published_at without re-indexing) or whose mentions carry no date is now read by its clock; and mention rows without an article row are no longer counted. Synthetic text yields 0 stories in the measured cells, so equality of stories rests on the unit oracle and the read digest. 28 tests: an oracle copy of the old read, boundary articles (first instant, last second, end instant), a tracemalloc growth bound, a per-statement chunk bound, the plan of the statement the read really issues, the deadline spy and a read that really runs out of time, StatementTimeout propagation. Report: audit-0.5.0/inputs/remeasure-stories-export/REPORT.md.
